title: HR onboarding, IT provisioning, attendance, leave & payroll
summary: 6-step onboarding (no logins), separate IT provisioning, staff badges, attendance flags against the duty roster, weekly days off and the public holiday calendar, supervisor leave routing, one-click payroll.
markdown:
# HR, provisioning, attendance, leave & payroll

## Onboarding wizard (§6.1, §6.3)

| Step | Call |
|---|---|
| 1 Demographics (CNIC required) | `POST /hr/employees` → `emp_number` `EMP-2026-0142`, status `Draft` |
| 2 Job & finance (department, designation, supervisor, salary, contract, shift) | `PATCH /hr/employees/{id}/steps/2` |
| 3 Qualifications & licence (PMDC/PNC) | `PATCH …/steps/3`, `POST …/qualifications` |
| 4 Financial config (visiting specialists) | none: the Billing Admin sets the OT split contract (decisions 56; [operating theater](operating-theater.md)); show that it is needed and who sets it |
| 5 Document vault (multipart: `file`, `doc_type`; PDF, JPEG or PNG; the `Photo` printed on the ID card a JPEG or PNG only) | `POST /hr/employees/{id}/documents` |
| 6 Finalize | `POST /hr/employees/{id}/submit` → `Awaiting_IT_Provisioning` |

Step 2 picks the department from `GET /admin/departments` and the supervisor from `GET /staff/lookup`.

`GET /hr/employees/{id}` returns `checklist {ready, missing[]}` — the DB refuses submission without a
CNIC document (`EMPLOYEE_DOCUMENT_REQUIRED`) or, for clinical staff, a licence number + document
(`CLINICAL_LICENSE_REQUIRED`). Step 6 **never creates a login**. Zero-interface support staff
(sweepers, janitors, guards) go straight to `Active` and only get a staff badge
(`POST /hr/employees/{id}/badges`: an RFID card, a QR badge printed on the ID card, or a biometric enrolment).
ID card: `GET /hr/employees/{id}/id-card` (it carries the printed badge as `badge`).

Each qualification is then verified with its primary source (the HEC or the university, the PMDC or PNC register), and
the personnel file gathers orientation, the job description, appraisals, training, the disciplinary background and the
health record: see [personnel records](personnel-records.md).

## IT provisioning (§6.2)

Super Admin: `GET /admin/provisioning-queue` → `POST /admin/users {"employee_id", "role_codes": ["clinical_specialist", "hospital_admin"]}`
→ username (suggested from the name) + **temporary password shown once**. The user must change it at
first login. HR cannot call this (403); the DB refuses logins for draft profiles and zero-interface staff.
Creating the login is the only way an awaiting profile becomes `Active`. HR changing the profile after handing it over
(making the person clinical staff, removing the licence number) stops it with `CLINICAL_LICENSE_REQUIRED`: HR completes
the profile first.

## Employment status (§6.2b, decisions 60)

The staff directory changes a handed-over employee's status with `POST /hr/employees/{id}/status {"status", "reason", "left_on"}`:

| The employee is | Allowed `status` | Otherwise |
|---|---|---|
| `Draft` | none: finish the wizard | `EMPLOYEE_STATUS_INVALID`, `details.next_step` the submit call |
| `Awaiting_IT_Provisioning` | `Suspended`, `Resigned`, `Terminated` | `Active`: `EMPLOYEE_STATUS_INVALID`, `details.next_step` `POST /admin/users` |
| `Active` | `Suspended`, `Resigned`, `Terminated` | |
| `Suspended` | `Active`, `Resigned`, `Terminated` | |
| `Resigned`, `Terminated` | `Active` (re-joining, an appeal), or the other of the two | `Suspended`: `EMPLOYEE_STATUS_INVALID` |

Suspending or a leaver deactivates the login, revokes its sessions and every badge at once. `Active` keeps the employee
number and the records and clears `left_on`, and it checks the vault again (`EMPLOYEE_DOCUMENT_REQUIRED`,
`CLINICAL_LICENSE_REQUIRED`: upload with `POST /hr/employees/{id}/documents`, then repeat). The login stays off until IT
re-enables it (`POST /admin/users/{user_id}/active`) and revoked badges stay revoked: issue new ones
(`POST /hr/employees/{id}/badges`). Someone IT never gave a login (not zero-interface staff) goes back to IT's queue
instead: the answer's `employment_status` is `Awaiting_IT_Provisioning` and IT is told (`hr.provisioning.requested`).

## Attendance (§6.4)

Badge scans at the staff entrance (`POST /badge-stations/scans`) become In/Out punches; where there is no
station, supervisors take roll call (`POST /rosters/roll-call`). The worker computes daily flags against the
day's schedule: the **rostered** shift, else the employee's default shift (`POST /hr/employees/{id}/shift`, for
staff on a fixed schedule) unless it is one of their own weekly days off or a public holiday, else a rest day
(`Present`, `Late`, `HalfDay`, `Absent`, `Leave`, `Holiday`, `Off`), and emits
`attendance.flagged` to HR and the supervisor. Staff planned on the roster get no default shift
(`shift_pattern_id: null`), so their rest days are not absences. A night shift's punches, including the morning
exit, count for the evening it started. HR views `GET /hr/attendance`, corrects with
`POST /hr/attendance/manual` (reasoned, audited). HR plans duty rosters for all staff (`roster.manage.all`):
[Duty rosters, roll call, badges & attendance](duty-rosters-and-attendance.md).

## Weekly days off and the holiday calendar (§6.4, §6.6)

The hospital works every day, Sundays included, so there is **no hospital-wide day off**: each person has their own
weekly rest day, and the rest days rotate through the week. Staff on a fixed schedule are not expected at work on
their **weekly days off** or on **public holidays**; those days are `Off` / `Holiday`, both paid (payroll deducts only
`Absent` and half of `HalfDay`).

* Weekly days off belong to the default shift and are required with it: `POST /hr/employees/{id}/shift
  {"shift_pattern_id", "effective_from", "weekly_off_days": [3]}` (ISO weekdays, 1 = Monday … 7 = Sunday; `[]` = works
  every day, see extra duty below). Onboarding does not set a shift: this call does, after step 2.
  `GET /hr/employees/{id}` shows today's `schedule` (`shift_pattern_id` null and `weekly_off_days` [] = roster only).
  The shift from `GET /hr/shift-patterns`.
* Staff on the roster rest on the days they are not rostered; the planners rotate those days
  ([duty rosters](duty-rosters-and-attendance.md): "repeat, moving everyone's days on", the week check).
* The **holiday calendar** is kept by HR **and** the Hospital Admin (permission `hr.holiday.manage`; either may
  add, rename, move or withdraw a holiday); everyone with a login reads it:

| Call | What |
|---|---|
| `GET /holidays?year=2026` (or `date_from` / `date_to`, `include_inactive`) | the calendar |
| `POST /holidays {"holidays": [{"holiday_date", "name", "notes"?}, …]}` | add the year's gazetted list at once: all or nothing; a taken date → `HOLIDAY_DATE_TAKEN` with `details.entry_index` |
| `PATCH /holidays/{id} {"expected_version", "name"?, "holiday_date"?, "notes"?, "is_active"?}` | rename / move / withdraw (`is_active: false`); never deleted |

* Nothing recurs: the Eids follow the moon, and the government's list changes, so enter each year's dates.
* Rostered staff work as rostered on a holiday (a hospital never closes); the roster planner marks the holidays
  (`GET /rosters/staff` → `holidays`). A person on the roster only is `Holiday` on a holiday they are not rostered.
* Adding or changing a holiday that is today or already past recomputes that day's flags at once. A payroll run
  already generated for the period is not changed: cancel it and generate it again.
* Leave is counted in calendar days (`leave_days`), so a holiday or weekly day off inside a leave uses a leave
  day, as in most Pakistani hospitals' leave rules.

## Leave (§6.5)

Employee: `POST /self/leave-requests {"leave_type", "from_date", "to_date", "half_day"?}` — checked
against the balance (`LEAVE_INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE`) and routed to the supervisor from step 2
(`leave.requested` + inbox). Supervisor (Head Nurse dashboard etc.): `GET /hr/leave-requests` →
`POST /hr/leave-requests/{id}/decision {"decision": "Approved"}`; the supervisor or HR (`hr.leave.manage`) decides,
anyone else gets `LEAVE_NOT_YOUR_REPORT`.

## Payroll (§6.6)

`POST /hr/payroll-runs {"period_start", "period_end"}` → per employee
**Base − Unpaid absences − Internal pharmacy/store credit + Accrued OT commissions + Extra duty = Net** (also a DB
constraint), with line items.

**Extra duty** (`extra_duty_days`, `extra_duty_pay`, payslip line `ExtraDuty` with the dates): each employee is due
`weekly_rest_days` days off per roster week (starting on `roster_week_start_day`). A **scheduled** duty (a roster entry
or the default shift) worked beyond the week's allowance, e.g. the seventh day of a week without a rest day, is paid
at `extra_duty_day_pay_rate` × a day's pay (base ÷ days in the period; half for a half day; 0 = not paid). Coming in
on a rest day without being rostered does not count: the roster manager rosters the person for it (HR also for a past
date), so every extra day paid has a named approver. An extra day is paid in the period of the date it was worked. Review → `POST …/{run_id}/finalize` (consumes credits/commissions, posts
the payroll journal) → `POST …/{run_id}/paid {"method": "BankTransfer"}`. Visiting consultants are paid
per case via AP, not payroll. Employees see payslips in `GET /self/profile` / `GET /self/payslips/{id}`.
